messages.author: ae8f0487533c97e5
messages.subject: Strange mapreduce failure with specific size of input array
parts:
Hi there,

I am getting the following error when executing MR from RHadoop. The error below is reported in container output. The job fails of cause after two retries.

Error: !is.null(template) is not TRUE

No traceback available 

Error during wrapup: 

Execution halted

Complete container output with error
Complete R STDOUT with error

R code to reproduce the problem(hopefully)

library(rmr2); library(rhdfs); hdfs.init()

rmr.options(backend = 'hadoop'
              ,backend.parameters = list(hadoop = list(
              D='mapreduce.job.maps=8'
             ))
            )

prime_mapper <- function(., numbers) {
  keyval(numbers, numbers)
}

crash.data.file = '/tmp/crash-data'
# crasher 24749991
if (dfs.exists(crash.data.file)) dfs.rmr(crash.data.file);
to.dfs(keyval(NULL, 1:24749991), output=crash.data.file)

input = from.dfs(input=crash.data.file)
length(input$val)

# generate summary of mined primes
output = mapreduce(input = crash.data.file, map = prime_mapper)
output_data = from.dfs(output)
length(output_data$val)

That snippet runs just fine when array size is set to 24749990. Please check links below...

Complete successful R stdout
Complete successful container output

All tests were run on Cloudera 5.3. 

Any thoughts how to work around it?
 
Thanks

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#1914] Strange mapreduce failure with specific size of input array
parts:
A workaround is hard to suggest not knowing exactly what the work is. In general, picking such a large number (compared to data size) of distinct keys is not an efficient pattern, but you could get away with it using a mapreduce feature called vectorized reduce, whereby each reduce call processes multiple groups. That said, the nice test case you provided should work and I intend to get to the bottom of this. Update: your test case just completed fine on my machine. I would first check that you have all your rmr2 copies up to the same version 3.3.1. I know it's pretty basic, but if you read some other threads you know it happens. Another thing is, I would be curious how you came to determine the specific number that causes this failure. Is it from this size up, is it just bad luck? Did you binary search for the critical number? Trying to learn if there is a pattern of failure.
Thanks

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#1924] Strange mapreduce failure with specific size of input array
parts:
Hi Alex,
your mapper takes about 3 G as it's writing out (not your fault, it's the design that's not really that great for very small records) so I am running out of memory before I can get to repro your problem. I need a bigger cluster. In the meantime, I'd be interested in knowing: how many map processes and reduce processes are actually running, how many bytes in and out for either type, particularly please look for reduce procs with small input size. The idea is that metadata is heavy for some data structures, so we don't repeat it for every record, but enough that every reducer should get a copy early on. We supported this approach with both analysis and experiments. It may be that there are some cases, e.g. very small record size, where the analysis is incorrect and the experiments insufficient.


Antonio
